newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HomeChoice in healthy debut on SAfrica JSE.
newsitem.headline: HomeChoice in healthy debut on SAfrica JSE.

text.p: Direct marketer, HomeChoice, made a healthy debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in busy dealings on Friday first trading at 240 cents a share, a 20 percent premium to its issue price.
But a steady stream of profit-taking by private and public investors knocked the share off its morning peak of 242 cents, to as low as 230 cents, dealers said.
"There were about 361,000 shares traded at 242 cents but then shares drifted back after a lot of private clients came in to offload stock to make a small profit," one dealer said.
HomeChoice managing director Rick Garratt said he was pleased with the listing and that the first day's trading had gone according to expectations.
"In talks with our merchant we estimated an opening range of 230 to 240 cents...It was expected to then drop as the stags began to sell off stock," Garratt told Reuters on Friday.
Traders said activity in the share had been characterised by many small deals.
"Trade has been in flows of 1,000 or 2,000 shares a time which is indicative of the man-in-the-street coming in. We haven't seen any big institutitional interest," a dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the share to close in a 230 to 234 cent range, rising back to around to 240 cents next week once stags were out of the market.

Sponsoring broker Investec Merchant Bank said on Friday the public offer of five million shares had been 7.1 times oversubscribed and the private placing of 18.5 million shares, 2.2 times oversubscribed.
The listing of the shares, issued at two rand each, raised 47 million rand.
HomeChoice, which is involved in the direct mail industry, said earlier this month it planned to expand its six sales offices to more than 20 over the next 18 months.
At 1120 GMT shares were trading at 232 cents after 1.4 million shares had changed hands in 221 deals.
